title: Rational-field tensors are polynomial localizations with Cohen–Macaulay local rings
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $F/k$ and $L/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], and let $r\geq0$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in F$ be algebraically independent over $k$, with $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$; here this notation means the smallest subfield containing $k$ and these elements, and algebraic independence means that evaluation $k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\to F$, $x_i\mapsto t_i$, is injective [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $P=L[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, let $W\subset P$ be the image of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\setminus\{0\}$ under coefficient inclusion, and put $A=F\otimes_kL$ with the usual algebra tensor multiplication [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is an $L$-algebra isomorphism $W^{-1}P\cong A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] sending $l x^\alpha/w$ to $(t^\alpha/w(t))\otimes l$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ its localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] satisfying $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), last two sentences of the proof: the rational-field tensor base is a localization of a polynomial ring and is Cohen–Macaulay.

proof.text: Put $B=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $S=B\setminus\{0\}$. Evaluation embeds $B$ into $F$. The subset $E=\{f(t)/s(t):f\in B,\ s\in S\}$ is a subfield of $F$: addition and multiplication use common denominators, and a nonzero fraction has inverse $s(t)/f(t)$ since injectivity gives $f\ne0$. It contains $k$ and every $t_i$, hence $E=F$ by the smallest-subfield hypothesis. The map $S^{-1}B\to F$, $f/s\mapsto f(t)/s(t)$, is therefore surjective and injective: equality of two images is precisely $(fs'-f's)(t)=0$, hence $fs'=f's$. It is a ring isomorphism. Coefficient inclusion $B\to P$ is injective by equality of polynomial coefficients, so its image $W$ of $S$ is multiplicatively closed and excludes zero.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), rational-field localization in the last two sentences of the proof; elementary fraction construction.

proof.text: Identify $C=B\otimes_k L$ with $P$ by $\theta(f\otimes l)=l f$, where $f$ on the right denotes coefficient inclusion. Its inverse sends $\sum_\alpha l_\alpha x^\alpha$ to $\sum_\alpha x^\alpha\otimes l_\alpha$. The formula for $\theta$ is bilinear over $k$; its inverse is additive. The composites are the identity on monomials with coefficients and on pure tensors, respectively, by $k$-balancing. These generate both modules. Products agree since $(x^\alpha\otimes l)(x^\beta\otimes m)=x^{\alpha+\beta}\otimes lm$, and $1\otimes l$ corresponds to the constant polynomial $l$. Thus this is an $L$-algebra isomorphism carrying the action of $s\in S$ to multiplication by its coefficient image in $W$.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), identification with the polynomial localization, expanded using polynomial coefficients and tensor bilinearity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its $R=k$, $A=B$, $T=S$, $M=B$, and $N=L$. Using step 1, it gives a bijective $B$-linear map $S^{-1}C\to F\otimes_k L$ with $(f\otimes l)/s\mapsto(f(t)/s(t))\otimes l$. Under step 2, $S^{-1}C=W^{-1}P$: the fraction relations coincide because the $S$-action on $C$ is multiplication by the corresponding element of $W$. This bijection is multiplicative: on fraction generators the product of $(f\otimes l)/s$ and $(g\otimes m)/u$ is $(fg\otimes lm)/(su)$, and their images multiply to $(f(t)g(t)/(s(t)u(t)))\otimes lm$. Additivity extends this equality to arbitrary fractions, since each numerator is a finite sum of pure tensors. The unit and $L$-action are respected by $1/1\mapsto1\otimes1$ and $(1\otimes l)/1\mapsto1\otimes l$. This proves the required $L$-algebra isomorphism and its asserted monomial-fraction formula.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), applied to the rational-field tensor in Tag 045M.

proof.text: The field $L$ is Noetherian: an ideal containing a nonzero $a$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$, so its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated. Its only prime ideal is $(0)$, and $L_{(0)}\cong L$ via $a/b\mapsto ab^{-1}$. There are no strict prime chains of positive length, so $\dim L=0$. The empty regular sequence exists in its maximal ideal $(0)$, while every nonempty sequence in $(0)$ starts with zero, whose multiplication on the nonzero module $L$ is not injective. Hence $\operatorname{depth}L=0$, and the same descriptions apply to $L_{(0)}$. Thus $L$ meets all the base-ring hypotheses of [lem-trf-polynomial-algebra-cm].

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), field base case for its use of Tag 00ND; elementary verification of the hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-algebra-cm] to $R=L$ and $n=r$. It gives that $P$ is Noetherian and that $\operatorname{depth}(P_{\mathfrak q})=\dim P_{\mathfrak q}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $P$ and $W$; its conditions hold for the fraction construction $D=W^{-1}P$. Consequently $D$, and therefore its isomorphic ring $A$ from step 3, is Noetherian (an isomorphism carries generators of each inverse-image ideal to generators).

source.place: Tag 00ND (lemma-CM-polynomial-algebra) and Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), as used in Tag 045M.

proof.text:
Identify $A$ with $D$ by step 3. Given a prime $\mathfrak p\subset D$, put $\mathfrak q=\{a\in P:a/1\in\mathfrak p\}$. This is prime by contraction, and $W\cap\mathfrak q=\varnothing$ since the elements of $W$ become units. There are inverse ring maps $P_{\mathfrak q}	o D_{\mathfrak p}$, $a/b\mapsto(a/1)/(b/1)$, and $D_{\mathfrak p}	o P_{\mathfrak q}$, $(a/w)/(b/v)\mapsto av/(wb)$. Indeed $b/v
otin\mathfrak p$ implies $b
otin\mathfrak q$, so $wb
otin\mathfrak q$; changing representatives preserves each map by the cross-multiplication relation for fractions. Substitution gives the identity for both composites. The definition of prime localization makes $D_{\mathfrak p}$ local, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. The displayed isomorphism carries prime chains bijectively and carries regular sequences in maximal ideals bijectively: multiplication on each successive quotient is conjugated by the induced isomorphism, and nonzero quotients stay nonzero. Thus it preserves both dimension and depth, so step 5 gives $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), last sentence; the local-ring identification is checked on fractions, and Tag 00FN gives Noetherianity.

lean.statement: theorem rationalField_localization_and_local_depth_eq_dimension (k : Type u) (F : Type v) (L : Type w) [Field k] [Field F] [Field L] [Algebra k F] [Algebra k L] (r : ℕ) (t : Fin r → F) (hind : Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval t : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k →ₐ[k] F)) (hgen : IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range t) = ⊤) : ∃ e : @AlgEquiv L (Localization ((nonZeroDivisors (MvPolynomial (Fin r) k)).map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k L)))) (F ⊗[k] L) _ _ _ _ (rightAlgebra (R := k) (A := F) (B := L)), (∀ (α : Fin r →₀ ℕ) (l : L) (s : nonZeroDivisors (MvPolynomial (Fin r) k)), e (Localization.mk (MvPolynomial.monomial α l) ⟨MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k L) s, ⟨s, s.property, rfl⟩⟩) = ((∏ i : Fin r, t i ^ α i) / MvPolynomial.aeval t (s : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k)) ⊗ₜ[k] l) ∧ IsNoetherianRing (F ⊗[k] L) ∧ ∀ (p : Ideal (F ⊗[k] L)) [p.IsPrime], IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ (IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime p) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p)
